mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which is typically associated with increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where the UNRATE drops by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals increased demand for housing and related goods, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increases by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face reduced output and potentially higher costs.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the periods where FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a combination of rising employment (PAYEMS) and falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and can result in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face higher labor costs.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where both PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a high level of real personal savings (RSAFS) above $700 billion signals strong consumer demand, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially in an economic expansion regime.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS is above $700 billion during an economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a combination of increasing industrial production (INDPRO) and decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from both increased demand and a more efficient labor market.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where both INDPRO increases by more than 1% and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month.
